column3: NASB has no “answering” and no “Jesus,” though the critical text has “answering”; “thrown down” is rendered “torn down.”
NASB renders “you will begin to hear” as “you will be hearing” and adds “those things” and “that”; it has no “all,” like the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text without “pestilences.”
“The love of the many” is rendered “most people’s love.”
NASB renders “the earth” (oikoumenē) as “the whole world” and “proclaimed” as “preached.”
NASB puts “let the reader understand” in parentheses.
NASB has no “also,” like the critical text.
NASB has no “for,” like the critical text.
Close to the Greek; the Old Testament wording is partly in capitals.
NASB renders “heaven” as “sky” in both places.
